beats.text: The villain? Static issue-derived tasks. They treat coding like a single-shot exam, ignoring the constant planning and refactoring we do.
beats.visual_focus: A single question mark morphing into a complex, tangled web of IDE interactions.

beats.text: Enter SWE-TaskFlow. It forces benchmarks to mirror real telemetry by steering agents through authentic, multi-step task sequences.
beats.visual_focus: A flow chart showing prompt splitting and repository QA alignment.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: The hook was solid—I hate how benchmarks don't reflect actual dev work, so you had me immediately. But you lost me in Beat 4. You dropped 'KL-divergence' out of nowhere without explaining why it matters for the agent's performance. It sounds like you're trying to sound smart for a paper rather than explaining the tech to a dev. Also, Beat 5 is a bit confusing—are you saying the cost is the 'result' or just a side effect?

thriller_metadata.physical_analogy: A single-shot exam trying to simulate a marathon of constant context-switching and planning.
thriller_metadata.paradigm_shift: Interaction protocols are now a primary dimension of evaluation.
